title: Learning Topological Interactions for Multi-Class Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A fully convolutional module detects pixels that violate containment or exclusion between classes and adds loss on them, trained end to end.
adaptation: Encode two rules. First, an inactive region must have a crack prediction within 5 px (an adjacency rule; 99% of train inactive regions satisfy it). Second, crack is excluded from padding and frame. Loss is applied only to violating pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: the best multi-label or gated arm + violation loss. Baseline: that arm. Metrics: inactive precision and IoU, number of inactive regions with no crack nearby. Kill if the inactive IoU gain is < 0.01.
evidence: R: validated on 2D and 3D, CT and ultrasound, private and public challenge data. The abstract page gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none. Skeleton Recall and clDice were single-class topology losses, not cross-class constraints.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL has hard class rules: inactive regions touch a crack (99% in train), crack and inactive never lie on padding or frame_edge. Cheapest form is an inference rule: drop predicted inactive components with no predicted crack within k px. Training form: exclusion penalty between inactive / crack and padding / frame_edge.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Inference rule on existing PF checkpoints, k chosen on val (0 GPU-h); then PF + exclusion term vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if val inactive precision gain < 0.03 or inactive recall falls > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Exclusions: crack/inactive outside cell area. Adjacency rule (inactive region must have crack within 5 px) built as a custom violation map since TI_Loss covers containment/exclusion only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm best of region/presence arms + violation loss; metric inactive precision and count of inactive regions without nearby crack; kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.01 over its base.
